questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to go on exchange to challenge myself personally and academically. I wanted to explore a new university and explore other cultures, and furthermore, challenge myself by living in another country.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had heard that Utrecht was a great city going on exchange. Furthermore, it is a welcoming city with nice people and a lot of different cultures.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find the information I needed, however, it was difficult to get the courses I wanted at Utrecht University. Otherwise, Utrecht University informed us in good time about welcome week and other opportunities to meet new people.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The first day after arrival, they held an information event for every exchange student at the faculty of science. Additionally, they made a really good welcome week, where I got to meet a lot of exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are different options for on campus housing. The most known company is SSH, which owns multiple buildings for housing on campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No meal plans, but a kitchen in my apartment for cooking.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus is very nice, because you live together with other exchange students. This helps a lot creating new bonds to exchange students and meeting new people. I can definetly recommend it!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration was very easy, I just signed some documents. However, getting approval for the courses were more difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Science office helped me a lot solving the problems I had with the courses and questions about the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At first, not very succesful. I had chosen some courses and 3 our of four courses were approved, but when I arrived the timeslots of the classes crashed, which resulted in some mess. Thereby, it was difficult to find other courses I could enrolled.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that the courses you choose do not crash with their timeslots. And make sure you have the pre-knowledge for the courses, otherwise they will not approve you for the course. Furthermore, the courses have different levels. The level 1 courses can have a lot of test during the period, while the level 3 courses have less of this.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were good, because you could choose between different levels. The level 1 courses can have a lot of test during the period, while the level 3 courses have less of this and group work instead. Some courses have attendance.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Seminars, lectures and self-study, so almost the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I was enrolled for:
Meet Your Brains 
Mathematics and programming 
Academic writing
Introduction to Dutch Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really recommend: Meet your brains, Academic writing and Introduction to Dutch law. 
I do not recommend: Mathematics and programming

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I rent a bike, which I was really glad I did. cost 22 euros pr month

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing less expensive than I expected, but living cost is the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many opportunities for clubs, sports and activities. This also applies in Utrecht in general. A lot of students have different clubs and activities that are available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is a big sport center at science campus called Olympos. Very good facilities with a lot of sports clubs to register for. This opens new opportunities to meet local people and other exchange students out of class.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the Netherlands and its beautiful cities. Furthermore, ESN plans a lot of different and nice trips to other cities. The Netherlands location makes it easy to travel around Europe yourself with friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adjust to the culture. It seems a lot like Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up as a member in different clubs and activities. Additionally, the Dutch people talk very easily to you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Dutch people really want to talk to you and are welcoming but direct.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing before coming, look at courses before going, but do not expect you will get them alle. Lastly, rent a bike, it makes it easy to go around.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I haven't answered above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The personal experience and growth, and improving my English a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding new friends and be in another country just yourself. It was nice to speak a lot of English and improve the language.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
